tagline.text: A cool mountain waterfall at the end of a pine-scented trail in Santa Fe

location.label: Location
location.text: Imugan village, Santa Fe, Nueva Vizcaya (about 10 minutes by tricycle from Santa Fe town)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (avoid the days right after rain)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,200 (excluding the round-trip bus from Manila; local transport, entrance and meals, estimated)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Manila (MNL), then overland

children.text: Imugan Falls is a waterfall at an elevation of about 1,000 m in Santa Fe, Nueva Vizcaya. A paved trail of about 30 minutes leads to it and the entrance fee is very low, so it pairs well with Dalton Pass for a day trip.

Imugan Falls is in the village of Imugan in Santa Fe, Nueva Vizcaya. One travel blog places it in the western section of the Caraballo Mountains. The Caraballo range lies between the Cordillera and Sierra Madre ranges and is a source of water for the Cagayan River. According to PhilAtlas, Imugan village sits at about 969 m above sea level and Santa Fe town at about 913 m, so coming up from Manila you will notice how much cooler the highlands are.
Sources differ slightly on the height of the falls. One blog describes a single-tier cascade of about 35 feet (roughly
), while the Wikipedia article on Santa Fe describes a two-level waterfall about

high. The water comes from a spring above on Mount Imugan, is cold, and collects in a shallow basin before flowing downstream. The same blog calls it the most famous waterfall in Nueva Vizcaya; it is best understood as a place loved for its easy access and pleasant setting rather than for sheer size.

Santa Fe is home to many Kalanguya (Ikalahan) people. According to Wikipedia, the Kalanguya are a minority group related to the Igorot, numbering about 14,500 in 2015, and in 1972 they founded the Kalahan Educational Foundation to secure their ancestral land. Imugan was also the former name of the town. Some visitors mention pine trees and cool air along the way to the falls. Santa Fe is the first town in Region 2 (Cagayan Valley) for travelers coming from Manila; it borders Pangasinan and sits in the Caraballo Mountains where Nueva Vizcaya and Nueva Ecija meet. Its population was about 18,950 in the 2024 census. Local products reported include brooms, strawberry jam, strawberry wine, peanut butter, orchids and quilts, so the shops in town are a good place to look for souvenirs.

Imugan Falls is not a big enough attraction to justify a long trip on its own. But buses from Manila to Isabela and Cagayan pass nearby and the Dalton Pass memorial is close, so it is a good place to set aside a day on a trip through northern Luzon. The trail is paved and signposted, so you can walk it without a guide. A review on the cycling app Komoot says you can ride a bicycle to the entrance. Distances reported vary: the village is about
6–7 km
from the national highway, and the most common description of the walk from the village to the falls is 15–30 minutes.

A waterfall about 11 m high drops into a shallow pool in dense forest. One blog says the water is clean, cold and not deep, making it good for swimming. However, one visitor reports that the current was strong enough to push the body and that a slipper was lost and then recovered, so take care in the pool.
The walk of about 1.5 km from the village road to the falls takes about 30 minutes at an easy pace. The path is paved and signposted, so it is easy to follow. A guide is reportedly not required.

blocks.title: Mount Imugan and the pine forest

children.text: The falls lie at the foot of Mount Imugan, which rises to about 1,700 m and is the highest point of Balete Ridge. Pine trees and cool air line the way. Morning is the best time for photos.

Around the barangay hall, where you register, there are small stores that sell drinks and snacks. One blog also mentions that fees are collected at the Caslangan Store nearby. Stop by before heading to the falls to ask about local conditions.
Imugan village is in the same town as the Dalton Pass memorial, so you can combine two sites in one day: the falls in the morning and the war history at the memorial in the afternoon.

blocks.title: A tour of Nueva Vizcaya waterfalls

children.text: A weekend itinerary suggested by one blog starts with Imugan Falls and continues to the Capisaan Caves, Antutut Falls and Edralin Falls, and Mapalyao Falls. It is a route through the province focused on waterfalls and caves.

There is a shelter in front of the falls, built in 2014, and a restroom installed by the local government is said to be close by. The rocks beside the pool serve as a picnic spot. Small falls can also be seen beside and below the main falls.

Besides the main trail built by the local government, a path leads to the top of the falls for adventurous visitors. A 2014 blog says the main falls has several levels and that most visitors climb up to level 2. It is wet and slippery above, so climb carefully.
Get off at the Santa Fe highway stop, hire a tricycle and go to Imugan village. It takes about 10 minutes.
Register and pay the entrance fee at the barangay hall. Arrange for the tricycle to wait for you or come back.
Walk the paved trail for about 30 minutes to reach the falls. It is quiet early in the morning.
Return to the village and take the tricycle back to the highway.
Have lunch in Santa Fe town, then go to Dalton Pass and look around the national shrine.
Check the time of the last bus to Manila and board.
One blog's weekend itinerary arrived in Santa Fe around 4:00 AM, took a tricycle at 6:00, reached Imugan at 6:15 and the falls at 6:45.

items.title: Two days, one night
items.subtitle: Waterfalls and caves in sequence from Santa Fe

children.text: Visit Imugan Falls.
Take a jeepney from Santa Fe to Bambang and buy water and food. The blog suggests transferring to a jeepney toward Kasibu and spending the night near the Capisaan Caves.
See Antutut Falls and Edralin Falls, then return to Manila via Solano.
Caves and distant waterfalls depend on jeepney schedules, so leave plenty of time in your plans.
Take a bus bound for Isabela or Cagayan from a northern Manila terminal and get off at Santa Fe. Blogs gave the fare as
and the travel time as
about 6–7 hours
(₱255 from a page updated in 2023, ₱285 from older posts). This is old information, so confirm the current fare and times at the terminal.

One blog names Victory, Florida and Dalin as bus companies. Look for a bus whose signboard reads Tuguegarao, Santiago, Isabela or Banaue; Santa Fe is the first town in Region 2 as you come from Manila. The travel time was given as
5–7 hours
Santa Fe town is about
205 km
from Manila by road according to a map service (Wikipedia says 309 km, so sources differ widely), and about
53 km
from the provincial capital, Bayombong.

items.title: From the Santa Fe highway to Imugan village

children.text: Blogs from 2014 and 2020 report public jeepneys leaving from the waiting shed in front of the Santa Fe municipal hall at 11:30, 13:00, 15:00 and 17:00. The fare was given as
per person (
for students). We could not re-confirm this schedule and fare in recent sources, so they may have changed. Confirm locally.
The tricycle ride from the highway to Imugan village takes about
10 minutes
. One blog gave the shared fare as
per person one way (₱30 in a 2023 post), and another source says
per tricycle. It varies with the number of passengers and negotiation.
From the village entrance to the falls it is about
1.5 km
on a paved path, or about
30 minutes
on foot.
The jump-off point is in the Halong area, where a signboard points to the falls. Walk back the same way.
Public transport from Imugan back to town is reportedly scarce. Ask your tricycle driver to wait for you or to come back and pick you up. This may raise the fare.
A recent review mentions a parking fee of
at the lot near the village entrance.
A Komoot review says you can also cycle to the entrance; the elevation is about 1,030 m, so allow for the climb.
According to Wikipedia, Santa Fe's average daily highs are
and lows are

. Wikipedia's climate table gives annual rainfall of about 897 mm and about 186 rainy days a year, but other climate sources differ widely, so treat it as a rough guide only. It is relatively cool even at midday because of the altitude, but some days are sunny and strong, so bring plenty of water.

The November–May dry season is the most comfortable for walking. Right after heavy rain the pool can be murky and the path slippery, so watch the weather. Going early means fewer people and cooler temperatures.

and may vary with local conditions.

Imugan village has small stores that reportedly sell drinks and snacks. One cycling review advises bringing your own food. Rather than counting on a meal in the village, it is safer to eat in Santa Fe town before you go.

For lodging, Santa Fe town or the provincial capital Bayombong (about 53 km away) are the realistic options. No specific business names or prices could be confirmed, so none are listed. One blog recommends buying water and food in Bambang.
Arrange your ride back (a tricycle that waits or comes to pick you up) before you go up.
Starting early means fewer people and a relaxed rest at the falls.
The trail is paved, but it is wet near the falls and you can slip, so non-slip footwear is a good idea.
Buy water and snacks in Santa Fe town beforehand.
Whether swimming is allowed and the entrance fee can change, so check the latest information at the barangay hall.
Combining the trip with the Dalton Pass memorial on the same day is efficient.
Bring plenty of small bills. Cards are unlikely to be accepted in the village.
A restroom installed by the local government is said to be near the falls, but its condition has not been confirmed, so take care of your needs before leaving the village.
Public transport from Imugan back to town is limited. If you do not arrange a ride back, you may have to walk out.
Entrance and transport fares differ between sources and must be confirmed locally. Most are old blog information.
Sources differ on the height and number of tiers (one or two tiers, about 11 m). Check for yourself on site.
The path and pool can be dangerous in the rainy season. It is better not to go on days of heavy rain.
A guide is reportedly not needed, but if it is your first time, ask a villager for directions once.
Carry your trash out and do not use soap or detergent in the pool.
The national shrine of the Battle of Balete Pass, in the same town of Santa Fe. A good afternoon stop after the falls.
Caves in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya; guides are reportedly arranged at the Capisaan Caves office in Kasibu.
Waterfalls in Antutut village, Kasibu, reached by jeepney. Check the schedule.
The World Heritage rice terraces of Ifugao to the north.
